claim: Dali is a conserved central nervous system expressed intergenic lncRNA.
source: Here, we report both genomically local and distal RNA-dependent roles of Dali, a conserved central nervous system expressed intergenic lncRNA.
evidence: The abstract directly states this characteristic of Dali, supported by subsequent experimental data showing CNS expression patterns.

claim: Dali is transcribed downstream of the Pou3f3 transcription factor gene.
source: Dali is transcribed downstream of the Pou3f3 transcription factor gene and its depletion disrupts the differentiation of neuroblastoma cells.
evidence: The abstract states this genomic relationship, which is confirmed by genomic mapping data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Depletion of Dali disrupts the differentiation of neuroblastoma cells.
source: Dali is transcribed downstream of the Pou3f3 transcription factor gene and its depletion disrupts the differentiation of neuroblastoma cells.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing reduced neurite outgrowth in Dali knockdown cells.

claim: Dali transcript regulates transcription of the Pou3f3 locus locally.
source: Locally, Dali transcript regulates transcription of the Pou3f3 locus.
evidence: This is demonstrated by qRT-PCR data showing reduced Pou3f3 expression upon Dali knockdown.

claim: Dali preferentially targets active promoters.
source: Distally, it preferentially targets active promoters and regulates expression of neural differentiation genes, in part through physical association with the POU3F3 protein.
evidence: CHART-seq data shows enrichment of Dali binding at regions with active chromatin marks (H3K4me3, H3K27ac, PolII).

claim: Dali regulates expression of neural differentiation genes.
source: Distally, it preferentially targets active promoters and regulates expression of neural differentiation genes, in part through physical association with the POU3F3 protein.
evidence: Microarray analysis shows that Dali knockdown affects expression of genes enriched in neural differentiation functions.

claim: Dali physically associates with the POU3F3 protein.
source: Distally, it preferentially targets active promoters and regulates expression of neural differentiation genes, in part through physical association with the POU3F3 protein.
evidence: UV-RIP experiments demonstrate direct RNA-protein interaction between Dali and FLAG-tagged POU3F3.

claim: Dali interacts with the DNMT1 DNA methyltransferase in mouse and human.
source: Dali interacts with the DNMT1 DNA methyltransferase in mouse and human and regulates DNA methylation status of CpG island-associated promoters in trans.
evidence: UV-RIP experiments in both mouse N2A and human SH-SY5Y cells confirm the interaction.

claim: Dali regulates DNA methylation status of CpG island-associated promoters in trans.
source: Dali interacts with the DNMT1 DNA methyltransferase in mouse and human and regulates DNA methylation status of CpG island-associated promoters in trans.
evidence: Bisulfite sequencing shows increased CpG methylation at Dali-bound promoters (Dlgap5, Hmgb2, Nos1) upon Dali depletion.

claim: A single intergenic lncRNA can control the activity and methylation of genomically distal regulatory elements to modulate large-scale transcriptional programmes.
source: These results demonstrate, for the first time, that a single intergenic lncRNA controls the activity and methylation of genomically distal regulatory elements to modulate large-scale transcriptional programmes.
evidence: This is supported by CHART-seq showing genome-wide Dali binding, microarray data showing widespread gene expression changes, and methylation analysis showing trans effects.

claim: Many intergenic lncRNA loci regulate the expression of adjacent protein coding genes.
source: Many intergenic long noncoding RNA (lncRNA) loci regulate the expression of adjacent protein coding genes.
evidence: This statement is presented as established knowledge in the abstract.

claim: It is unclear whether intergenic lncRNAs commonly regulate transcription by modulating chromatin at genomically distant loci.
source: Less clear is whether intergenic lncRNAs commonly regulate transcription by modulating chromatin at genomically distant loci.
evidence: This is presented as a knowledge gap that the study addresses.

claim: Many nuclear localised lncRNAs regulate gene transcription and chromatin organisation.
source: A growing number of nuclear localised long noncoding RNAs (lncRNA, ≥ 200 nt) are known to regulate gene transcription and chromatin organisation (reviewed in (Vance and Ponting, 2014)).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a review article.

claim: Many nuclear lncRNAs appear to act near to their site of synthesis to regulate the expression of genes locally on the same chromosome (cis-acting).
source: Many of these transcripts appear to act near to their site of synthesis to regulate the expression of genes locally on the same chromosome (cis-acting).
evidence: This is presented as established knowledge from the literature.

claim: Cis-acting lncRNA regulatory mechanisms have been described in detail for enhancer associated nuclear lncRNAs, as well as lncRNAs involved in genomic imprinting and X chromosome inactivation.
source: Cis-acting lncRNA regulatory mechanisms have been described in detail for a number of enhancer associated nuclear lncRNAs, as well as lncRNAs involved in the processes of genomic imprinting and X chromosome inactivation (Tian et al., 2010; Melo et al., 2013; Monnier et al., 2013; Mousavi et al., 2013; Santoro et al., 2013; Vallot et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to published studies.

claim: Some cis-acting lncRNAs bind to DNA methyltransferase (DNMT) proteins and regulate genomic DNA methylation levels specifically at their sites of transcription.
source: Some cis-acting lncRNAs bind to DNA methyltransferase (DNMT) proteins and regulate genomic DNA methylation levels specifically at their sites of transcription (Mohammad et al., 2010; Di Ruscio et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: Trans-acting lncRNAs that regulate gene expression across multiple chromosomes and on either allele have been documented less frequently.
source: Trans-acting lncRNAs that regulate gene expression across multiple chromosomes and on either allele have been documented less frequently.
evidence: This is presented as an observation about the state of the field.

claim: The ability of trans-acting lncRNAs to exert widespread effects on gene expression is poorly understood.
source: The ability of such lncRNAs to exert widespread effects on gene expression in trans is poorly understood, in large part because direct transcriptional targets for only very few of these transcripts have thus far been identified (Chu et al., 2011; Ng et al., 2013; Simon et al., 2011; Vance et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations indicating limited examples in the literature.

claim: It is not clear whether trans-acting lncRNAs commonly act directly, or within ribonucleoprotein complexes.
source: Moreover, it is not clear whether these transcripts commonly act directly, or within ribonucleoprotein complexes, and how they might modify their target genes' regulatory landscape such as by regulating their DNA methylation profiles.
evidence: This is presented as a knowledge gap in the field.

claim: Many thousand mammalian intergenic lncRNAs have now been identified.
source: Many thousand mammalian intergenic lncRNAs have now been identified.
evidence: This is presented as established knowledge about the field.

claim: Not all lncRNA transcript models will be functional.
source: Not all lncRNA transcript models will be functional, however.
evidence: This is presented as a general principle based on understanding of the field.

claim: Single exon lncRNA models can be artefacts arising from genomic DNA contaminating sequencing libraries.
source: Single exon models, in particular, can be artefacts arising from genomic DNA contaminating sequencing libraries, and transcripts that are expressed at average levels lower than one copy per cell are less likely to confer function.
evidence: This is presented as a known technical issue in the field.

claim: Transcripts expressed at average levels lower than one copy per cell are less likely to confer function.
source: Single exon models, in particular, can be artefacts arising from genomic DNA contaminating sequencing libraries, and transcripts that are expressed at average levels lower than one copy per cell are less likely to confer function.
evidence: This is presented as a general principle about functional requirements.

claim: Neat1 and Malat1/Neat2 knockout mouse models are viable and fertile.
source: Highly and broadly expressed, and bona fide monoexonic intergenic lncRNAs, such as Neat1 and Malat1/Neat2, however, appear not to have essential roles because their knockout mouse models are viable and fertile (Eissmann et al., 2012; Zhang et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published knockout studies.

claim: Transcript sequences and levels are not reliable predictors of lncRNA mechanism.
source: Transcript sequences and levels are thus not reliable predictors of mechanism.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that highly expressed lncRNAs like Neat1 and Malat1 are not essential.

claim: The significant temporal and spatial co-expression of genomically adjacent intergenic lncRNA and transcription factor genes might suggest that such lncRNAs commonly modulate transcriptional programmes that are initiated by these transcription factors.
source: Instead, the significant temporal and spatial co-expression of genomically adjacent intergenic lncRNA and transcription factor genes might suggest that such lncRNAs commonly modulate transcriptional programmes that are initiated by these transcription factors (Ponjavic et al., 2009).
evidence: This is a hypothesis supported by citation to a study showing co-expression patterns.

claim: Several intergenic lncRNAs have well-documented cis-acting regulatory roles.
source: Indeed, several intergenic lncRNAs have well-documented cis-acting regulatory roles (Wang et al., 2011; Zhang et al., 2012; Berghoff et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: Spatiotemporal co-expression of intergenic lncRNA and transcription factor genes is most pronounced during the development of the mouse central nervous system (CNS).
source: Spatiotemporal co-expression of intergenic lncRNA and transcription factor genes is most pronounced during the development of the mouse central nervous system (CNS) (Ponjavic et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a published study.

claim: Dali is a 3.5-kb, CNS-expressed, monoexonic, intergenic lncRNA.
source: To investigate the mechanistic basis of this physical linkage we chose to study a 3.5-kb, CNS-expressed, monoexonic, intergenic lncRNA termed Dali (DNMT1-Associated Long Intergenic), owing to its conservation of sequence and transcription across therian mammals and its genomic proximity to a transcription factor gene, Pou3f3 (also known as Brn1 or Oct8), which encodes a class III POU family transcription factor.
evidence: This is based on characterization data including RACE and expression analysis.

claim: Dali sequence and transcription are conserved across therian mammals.
source: To investigate the mechanistic basis of this physical linkage we chose to study a 3.5-kb, CNS-expressed, monoexonic, intergenic lncRNA termed Dali (DNMT1-Associated Long Intergenic), owing to its conservation of sequence and transcription across therian mammals and its genomic proximity to a transcription factor gene, Pou3f3 (also known as Brn1 or Oct8), which encodes a class III POU family transcription factor.
evidence: This is supported by identification of orthologous transcripts in mouse, human, and rat.

claim: Dali is in genomic proximity to the Pou3f3 transcription factor gene.
source: To investigate the mechanistic basis of this physical linkage we chose to study a 3.5-kb, CNS-expressed, monoexonic, intergenic lncRNA termed Dali (DNMT1-Associated Long Intergenic), owing to its conservation of sequence and transcription across therian mammals and its genomic proximity to a transcription factor gene, Pou3f3 (also known as Brn1 or Oct8), which encodes a class III POU family transcription factor.
evidence: This is shown by genomic mapping data in Figure 1A.

claim: Pou3f3 encodes a class III POU family transcription factor.
source: To investigate the mechanistic basis of this physical linkage we chose to study a 3.5-kb, CNS-expressed, monoexonic, intergenic lncRNA termed Dali (DNMT1-Associated Long Intergenic), owing to its conservation of sequence and transcription across therian mammals and its genomic proximity to a transcription factor gene, Pou3f3 (also known as Brn1 or Oct8), which encodes a class III POU family transcription factor.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the Pou3f3 gene.

claim: Dali is transcribed in the sense orientation, relative to Pou3f3, from a locus 50 kb downstream of Pou3f3.
source: Dali is transcribed in the sense orientation, relative to Pou3f3, from a locus 50 kb downstream of Pou3f3 within the flank of an extended genomic region (Figure 1A) that is characterised by near pervasive transcription in neuronal lineages (Ramos et al., 2013).
evidence: This is shown by genomic mapping in Figure 1A and supported by citation.

claim: The Pou3f3 genomic region is characterised by near pervasive transcription in neuronal lineages.
source: Dali is transcribed in the sense orientation, relative to Pou3f3, from a locus 50 kb downstream of Pou3f3 within the flank of an extended genomic region (Figure 1A) that is characterised by near pervasive transcription in neuronal lineages (Ramos et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a published study.

claim: Genomic deletion of the linc-Brn1b locus resulted in significant (~50%) down-regulation of the upstream Pou3f3 gene.
source: Genomic deletion of the linc-Brn1b locus resulted in significant (∼50%) down-regulation of the upstream Pou3f3 gene, and linc-Brn1b-/- mice exhibited abnormalities of cortical lamination and barrel cortex organization (Sauvageau et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a published study.

claim: linc-Brn1b-/- mice exhibited abnormalities of cortical lamination and barrel cortex organization.
source: Genomic deletion of the linc-Brn1b locus resulted in significant (∼50%) down-regulation of the upstream Pou3f3 gene, and linc-Brn1b-/- mice exhibited abnormalities of cortical lamination and barrel cortex organization (Sauvageau et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a published study.

claim: The Dali locus does not overlap previously described lncRNA loci or regulatory elements.
source: The Dali locus is more distally located and does not overlap previously described lncRNA loci or regulatory elements (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is shown by genomic annotation in Figure 1A.

claim: Full-length mouse Dali is approximately 500 nt (2.6 kb) longer than a previously identified AK034039 cDNA cloned from the telencephalon.
source: Full-length mouse Dali is approximately 500 nt (2.6 kb) longer than a previously identified AK034039 cDNA cloned from the telencephalon (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is based on RACE mapping data shown in the figure supplement.

claim: The Dali locus contains mammalian conserved sequence both just upstream of its transcriptional start site and within its transcribed sequence.
source: Its locus, downstream of the Pou3f3 gene, contains mammalian conserved sequence both just upstream of its transcriptional start site, which presumably contributes to this locus' promoter, and within its transcribed sequence.
evidence: This is shown by conservation tracks in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: A positionally equivalent and sequence-similar human DALI (~3.7 kb) transcript was identified by RT-PCR and RACE in human foetal brain.
source: A positionally equivalent and sequence-similar human DALI (∼3.7 kb) transcript was identified by RT-PCR and RACE in human foetal brain (Figure 1B; Figure 1—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: This is based on experimental RACE data shown in the figures.

claim: Transcriptional evidence exists for the orthologous Dali locus in rat embryonic, heart and kidney samples.
source: Transcriptional evidence also exists for the orthologous locus in rat embryonic, as well as heart and kidney, samples (data not shown).
evidence: This is stated based on unpublished data.

claim: Both mouse and human Dali loci have the properties of a weak (or poised) enhancer in both brain and kidney tissues.
source: ENCODE data indicate that both mouse and human Dali loci have the properties of a weak (or poised) enhancer in both brain and kidney tissues (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D,E).
evidence: This is based on ENCODE chromatin state annotations shown in the figure supplement.

claim: Dali was most highly expressed in the adult brain and kidney, two of the three tissues displaying highest Pou3f3 expression.
source: Consistent with this, Dali was most highly expressed in the adult brain and kidney, two of the three tissues displaying highest Pou3f3 expression, when profiled across a panel of adult mouse organs (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F,G).
evidence: This is based on qRT-PCR data shown in the figure supplement.

claim: In adult mouse (P56), Dali and Pou3f3 were expressed in all three regions of adult neurogenesis: the sub-ventricular zone (SVZ), olfactory bulb (OB), and dentate gyrus (DG).
source: In adult mouse (P56), Dali and Pou3f3 were expressed in all three regions of adult neurogenesis, the sub-ventricular zone (SVZ), olfactory bulb (OB), and dentate gyrus (DG) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1I) (Reviewed in Ming and Song, 2011).
evidence: This is based on qRT-PCR data shown in the figure supplement.

claim: Dali was co-expressed with Pou3f3 temporally and spatially in the developing mouse embryonic brain.
source: Dali was also co-expressed with Pou3f3 temporally and spatially in the developing mouse embryonic brain (Figure 1C,D).
evidence: This is shown by qRT-PCR data in Figure 1C,D.

claim: Both Dali and Pou3f3 transcripts were up-regulated with the first appearance of cortical neurons (E10.5).
source: Both transcripts were up-regulated with the first appearance of cortical neurons (E10.5), and increased in expression further as the ratio between neurons and progenitors grew (Figure 1C,D).
evidence: This is shown by qRT-PCR data in Figure 1C,D.

claim: Both Dali and Pou3f3 transcripts were undetectable in self-renewing mouse E14 embryonic stem (ES) cells.
source: Furthermore, both Dali and Pou3f3 transcripts were undetectable in self-renewing mouse E14 embryonic stem (ES) cells, but after 3 days of retinoic acid (RA)-induced differentiation, a stage corresponding to the cell cycle exit of neuronal progenitors and their differentiation into neurons, these transcripts were rapidly up-regulated, their levels subsequently peaking at days 7 (Pou3f3) and 8 (Dali) (Figure 1E,F).
evidence: This is shown by qRT-PCR data in Figure 1E,F.

claim: After 3 days of retinoic acid (RA)-induced differentiation of ES cells, Dali and Pou3f3 transcripts were rapidly up-regulated, their levels subsequently peaking at days 7 (Pou3f3) and 8 (Dali).
source: Furthermore, both Dali and Pou3f3 transcripts were undetectable in self-renewing mouse E14 embryonic stem (ES) cells, but after 3 days of retinoic acid (RA)-induced differentiation, a stage corresponding to the cell cycle exit of neuronal progenitors and their differentiation into neurons, these transcripts were rapidly up-regulated, their levels subsequently peaking at days 7 (Pou3f3) and 8 (Dali) (Figure 1E,F).
evidence: This is shown by qRT-PCR data in Figure 1E,F.

claim: Mouse neuroblastoma N2A cells express both Dali (at a population-average level of 2 copies per cell) and Pou3f3.
source: Mouse neuroblastoma N2A cells, which are frequently used as a neuronal progenitor-like cell type and an in vitro model of neuronal differentiation (Tremblay et al., 2010), express both Dali (at a population-average level of 2 copies per cell (Figure 1—figure supplement 1K)) and Pou3f3.
evidence: This is based on qRT-PCR quantification shown in the figure supplement.

claim: When first detected in neuronal-progenitor-dominated areas of the developing brain (E10.5), Dali is expressed at a level at least two orders of magnitude higher than in N2A cells.
source: When first detected in neuronal-progenitor-dominated areas of the developing brain (E10.5), Dali is expressed at a level at least two orders of magnitude higher than in N2A cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: This is shown by qRT-PCR comparison data in the figure supplement.

claim: In N2A cells treated with RA for 72 hr, Dali is up-regulated approximately 4.5-fold.
source: However, in N2A cells treated with RA for 72 hr, Dali is up-regulated approximately 4.5-fold, similar to the up-regulation observed in embryonic cortical plate (both dorsal and lateral) between days E10.5 to E18.5 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: This is shown by qRT-PCR data in the figure supplement.

claim: N2A cells represent an appropriate model system in which to study Dali function.
source: Therefore, despite Dali expression level differences in N2A cells and the in vivo system, N2A cells represent an appropriate model system in which to study Dali function.
evidence: This is inferred from the similar fold-change in Dali expression during differentiation in N2A cells and in vivo.

claim: Dali, but not a control mRNA (Gapdh), was highly enriched in the nucleus of N2A cells, most abundantly in the chromatin fraction.
source: Furthermore, Dali, but not a control mRNA (Gapdh), was highly enriched in the nucleus of N2A cells, most abundantly in the chromatin fraction (Figure 1G,H).
evidence: This is shown by biochemical fractionation and qRT-PCR data in Figure 1G,H.

claim: Dali may be involved in regulating nuclear function during neuronal development, potentially in coordination with Pou3f3.
source: Taken together, the data suggest that Dali may be involved in regulating nuclear function during neuronal development, potentially in coordination with Pou3f3.
evidence: This is inferred from the co-expression patterns and nuclear localization of Dali.

claim: Compared to a stable non-targeting control line, fewer differentiated cells of Dali knockdown lines developed neurites.
source: Compared to a stable non-targeting control line, fewer differentiated cells of Dali knockdown lines developed neurites.
evidence: This is shown by neurite outgrowth quantification in Figure 2B,C.

claim: Differentiated Dali knockdown cells that developed neurites exhibited shorter neurites, often with multiple short outgrowths emanating from the same cell, compared to one or two long neurites developed by differentiated control cells.
source: Those that did exhibited shorter neurites, often with multiple short outgrowths emanating from the same cell, compared to one or two long neurites developed by differentiated control cells (Figure 2B,C) indicating that Dali is required for normal differentiation of N2A cells.
evidence: This is shown by microscopy images and quantification in Figure 2B,C.

claim: Dali is required for normal differentiation of N2A cells.
source: Those that did exhibited shorter neurites, often with multiple short outgrowths emanating from the same cell, compared to one or two long neurites developed by differentiated control cells (Figure 2B,C) indicating that Dali is required for normal differentiation of N2A cells.
evidence: This is inferred from the neurite outgrowth defects observed upon Dali knockdown.

claim: Dali knockdown resulted in statistically significant changes in expression levels for 270 genes (False Discovery Rate [FDR] < 10%).
source: Dali knockdown resulted in statistically significant changes in expression levels for 270 genes (False Discovery Rate [FDR] < 10%) compared to a non-targeting control (Supplementary file 2; Figure 2E).
evidence: This is based on microarray analysis shown in Figure 2E.

claim: 14 of 15 genes identified as differentially expressed by microarray were also determined as being differentially expressed, with similar fold changes, using RT-qPCR and two additional independent shRNA expression constructs targeting Dali.
source: 14 of 15 of these genes were also determined as being differentially expressed, with similar fold changes, using RT-qPCR and two additional independent shRNA expression constructs targeting Dali (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is shown by validation data in the figure supplement.

claim: Gene expression changes observed using microarrays were unlikely to be dominated by off-target effects of the shRNA used.
source: Gene expression changes we observed using microarrays were thus unlikely to be dominated by off-target effects of the shRNA used.
evidence: This is inferred from the validation with multiple independent shRNAs showing similar results.

claim: Dali-regulated genes were significantly enriched in cell cycle, DNA repair, cellular response to stimulus, and cell projection assembly functions.
source: Gene Ontology (GO) analysis revealed that Dali-regulated genes were significantly enriched in cell cycle, DNA repair, cellular response to stimulus, and cell projection assembly functions (Figure 2F and Supplementary file 2; Benjamini-Hochberg corrected p ≤ 0.05).
evidence: This is based on GO enrichment analysis shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Dali acts as a pro-differentiation factor in neural development.
source: Taken together, these expression and loss of function studies suggest that Dali acts as a pro-differentiation factor in neural development.
evidence: This is inferred from the expression patterns and differentiation defects upon knockdown.

claim: Reduction of Dali levels by an average of 60–70% was found to reduce Pou3f3 transcript levels by approximately 40%.
source: After 72 hr, reduction of Dali levels by an average of 60–70% was found to reduce Pou3f3 transcript levels by approximately 40% (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is shown by qRT-PCR data in Figure 2G.

claim: Three independent stable Dali knockdown clones in which Dali levels were reduced by 50–60% showed ~15–40% lower Pou3f3 levels.
source: Three independent stable Dali knockdown clones in which Dali levels were reduced by 50–60% (Figure 2A) also showed ∼15–40% lower Pou3f3 levels (Figure 2H).
evidence: This is shown by qRT-PCR data in Figure 2A and 2H.

claim: The Dali transcript positively regulates Pou3f3 expression in an RNA-dependent manner.
source: This suggests that the Dali transcript positively regulates Pou3f3 expression in an RNA-dependent manner.
evidence: This is inferred from the reduction in Pou3f3 levels upon Dali knockdown.

claim: The genome-wide transcriptional response to Dali knockdown could be explained, in part, by its effect on Pou3f3.
source: The genome-wide transcriptional response to Dali knockdown thus could be explained, in part, by its effect on Pou3f3.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Dali regulates Pou3f3 expression.

claim: Levels of AK011913 were reduced by approximately 55% upon Dali knockdown.
source: Levels of another transcript, AK011913, expressed downstream of Pou3f3 (Figure 1A) were reduced by approximately 55% upon Dali knockdown (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is shown by qRT-PCR data in the figure supplement.

claim: Reduction of AK011913 levels by approximately 60% using shRNAs resulted in Dali and Pou3f3 levels decreasing by 73% and 82%, respectively.
source: Reduction of AK011913 levels by approximately 60% using shRNAs resulted in Dali and Pou3f3 levels decreasing by 73% and 82%, respectively (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is shown by qRT-PCR data in the figure supplement.

claim: Linc-Brn1a was up-regulated by approximately 90% upon AK011913 depletion.
source: Linc-Brn1a, a lncRNA upstream of and sharing a bi-directional promoter with Pou3f3, was up-regulated by approximately 90% upon AK011913 depletion (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is shown by qRT-PCR data in the figure supplement.

claim: Non-coding transcripts expressed from the extended Pou3f3 locus contribute to a complex network of regulatory interactions.
source: Together with previous reports, our data show the opposing regulatory influences of lncRNAs transcribed up- and downstream of Pou3f3 on its expression. Non-coding transcripts expressed from the extended Pou3f3 locus thus contribute to a complex network of regulatory interactions.
evidence: This is inferred from the multiple regulatory relationships observed between lncRNAs and Pou3f3.

claim: The Dali promoter contacted three regions across the Pou3f3 locus in ES derived neuronal precursors.
source: Furthermore, Chromatin Conformation Capture (3C) showed that the Dali promoter contacted three regions across the Pou3f3 locus (Figure 1A) in ES derived neuronal precursors (Figure 1—figure supplement 2)
evidence: This is shown by 3C data in the figure supplement.

claim: The Dali promoter contacts an enhancer element sequence lying upstream of Pou3f3 within the linc-Brn1a locus.
source: : 1) an enhancer element sequence lying upstream of Pou3f3 within the linc-Brn1a locus, 2) a region overlapping the 3′ UTR of Pou3f3 and full-length AK53590 (which are both regulated by Dali), as well as parts of TCONS_00000039 and linc-Brn1b, including a differentially methylated region reported to be important in regulating Pou3f3 expression (Mutai et al., 2009), and 3) a region lying within another non-coding locus (TCONS_00000040) (Ramos et al., 2013).
evidence: This is shown by 3C data in the figure supplement.

claim: The Dali promoter contacts a region overlapping the 3′ UTR of Pou3f3 and full-length AK53590, as well as parts of TCONS_00000039 and linc-Brn1b, including a differentially methylated region reported to be important in regulating Pou3f3 expression.
source: : 1) an enhancer element sequence lying upstream of Pou3f3 within the linc-Brn1a locus, 2) a region overlapping the 3′ UTR of Pou3f3 and full-length AK53590 (which are both regulated by Dali), as well as parts of TCONS_00000039 and linc-Brn1b, including a differentially methylated region reported to be important in regulating Pou3f3 expression (Mutai et al., 2009), and 3) a region lying within another non-coding locus (TCONS_00000040) (Ramos et al., 2013).
evidence: This is shown by 3C data and supported by citation.

claim: The Dali promoter contacts a region lying within another non-coding locus (TCONS_00000040).
source: : 1) an enhancer element sequence lying upstream of Pou3f3 within the linc-Brn1a locus, 2) a region overlapping the 3′ UTR of Pou3f3 and full-length AK53590 (which are both regulated by Dali), as well as parts of TCONS_00000039 and linc-Brn1b, including a differentially methylated region reported to be important in regulating Pou3f3 expression (Mutai et al., 2009), and 3) a region lying within another non-coding locus (TCONS_00000040) (Ramos et al., 2013).
evidence: This is shown by 3C data and supported by citation.

claim: Neither Dali nor Pou3f3 appears to play a role in initiating DNA looping interactions at the Pou3f3 locus because these contacts were present in E14 ES cells where neither is expressed.
source: Neither Dali nor Pou3f3 appears to play a role in initiating these DNA looping interactions because these contacts were present in E14 ES cells where neither is expressed (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is shown by 3C data in ES cells shown in the figure supplement.

claim: The Dali locus appears to contribute to an extended structurally and transcriptionally complex region centred on the Pou3f3 gene.
source: Nevertheless, the Dali locus appears to contribute to an extended structurally and transcriptionally complex region centred on the Pou3f3 gene.
evidence: This is inferred from the 3C data showing multiple contacts and the complex regulatory relationships.

claim: Pou3f3 knockdown resulted in statistically significant expression changes in 1041 genes (FDR <10%).
source: To examine to what extent the transcriptional response to Dali knockdown can be explained by its effect on Pou3f3, we reduced the level of Pou3f3 transcript in N2A cells by 35% using transient transfection of a Pou3f3 targeting shRNA vector (Figure 3A) and using microarrays observed statistically significant expression changes in 1041 genes (FDR <10%; Figure 3B).
evidence: This is shown by microarray data in Figure 3B.

claim: Dali transcript levels do not change upon Pou3f3 depletion.
source: Dali transcript levels do not change upon Pou3f3 depletion (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is shown by qRT-PCR data in Figure 3A.

claim: Genes differentially expressed after Pou3f3 knockdown were enriched in categories related to cell division and cell cycle.
source: Genes differentially expressed after Pou3f3 knockdown were enriched in categories related to cell division and cell cycle (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is shown by GO enrichment analysis in Figure 3C.

claim: The intersection between the sets of genes differentially expressed in Dali or in Pou3f3 knockdown cells was 6.2-fold greater than expected by chance (p-value < 2.2 × 10−16), and represented 31% of all genes differentially expressed in Dali knockdown cells.
source: The intersection between the sets of genes differentially expressed in Dali or in Pou3f3 knockdown cells was 6.2-fold greater than expected by chance (p-value < 2.2 × 10−16), and represented 31% of all genes differentially expressed in Dali knockdown cells (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is shown by Venn diagram analysis in Figure 3D.

claim: Approximately equal numbers of genes shared between Dali and Pou3f3 knockdown datasets were down- (43 genes) or up-regulated (41 genes) in both experiments.
source: Approximately equal numbers of genes shared between the two datasets were down- (43 genes) or up-regulated (41 genes) in both experiments (Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This is based on analysis of the microarray data.

claim: A strong correlation was observed between the fold-change values of differentially expressed genes in Dali and Pou3f3 knockdown experiments (R = 0.74).
source: A strong correlation was observed between the fold-change values of differentially expressed genes in Dali and Pou3f3 knockdown experiments (R = 0.74; Figure 3E).
evidence: This is shown by correlation analysis in Figure 3E.

claim: Genes that were significantly differentially expressed only when Dali was depleted were enriched in chromatin assembly and MAPKKK signalling functions.
source: Genes that were significantly differentially expressed only when Dali was depleted were enriched in chromatin assembly and MAPKKK signalling functions, whilst genes that were differentially expressed only when Pou3f3 transcripts were depleted were preferentially involved in dendrite development and axon guidance (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is shown by GO enrichment analysis in Figure 3F.

claim: Genes that were differentially expressed only when Pou3f3 transcripts were depleted were preferentially involved in dendrite development and axon guidance.
source: Genes that were significantly differentially expressed only when Dali was depleted were enriched in chromatin assembly and MAPKKK signalling functions, whilst genes that were differentially expressed only when Pou3f3 transcripts were depleted were preferentially involved in dendrite development and axon guidance (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is shown by GO enrichment analysis in Figure 3F.

claim: Cell cycle, DNA repair, and cellular response to stimulus genes were regulated by Dali in both Pou3f3-dependent and -independent manners.
source: Cell cycle, DNA repair, and cellular response to stimulus genes were regulated by Dali in both Pou3f3-dependent and -independent manners.
evidence: This is inferred from the GO enrichment analysis showing these categories in both shared and Dali-specific gene sets.

claim: Dali and Pou3f3 interact, either genetically or molecularly, to regulate a subset of common targets involved in neural differentiation.
source: We conclude that Dali and Pou3f3 interact, either genetically or molecularly, to regulate a subset of common targets involved in neural differentiation, and that Dali also likely possesses Pou3f3-independent transcriptional regulatory functions.
evidence: This is inferred from the significant overlap in target genes and correlation in expression changes.

claim: Dali likely possesses Pou3f3-independent transcriptional regulatory functions.
source: We conclude that Dali and Pou3f3 interact, either genetically or molecularly, to regulate a subset of common targets involved in neural differentiation, and that Dali also likely possesses Pou3f3-independent transcriptional regulatory functions.
evidence: This is inferred from the existence of genes regulated by Dali but not by Pou3f3.

claim: In proliferating cells, 733 genes were differentially expressed between Dali knockdown and control cells.
source: In proliferating cells, 733 genes were differentially expressed between Dali knockdown and control cells (Figure 4A), including many genes with functions related to neuronal differentiation, apoptosis, neuronal function (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is shown by microarray data in Figure 4A.

claim: RA-mediated neuronal differentiation induced expression changes in 958 genes in control cells and 1016 genes in Dali knockdown cells.
source: RA-mediated neuronal differentiation induced expression changes in 958 genes in control cells and 1016 genes in Dali knockdown cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This is shown by microarray data in the figure supplement.

claim: 804 genes were differentially expressed between terminally differentiated control and Dali knockdown cells.
source: However, 804 genes were differentially expressed between terminally differentiated control and Dali knockdown cells (Figure 4C), of which 376 genes (46.8%) also differed in expression between Dali knockdown and control cells prior to their differentiation (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is shown by microarray data in Figure 4C.

claim: 376 genes (46.8%) that were differentially expressed between differentiated Dali knockdown and control cells also differed in expression between Dali knockdown and control cells prior to their differentiation.
source: However, 804 genes were differentially expressed between terminally differentiated control and Dali knockdown cells (Figure 4C), of which 376 genes (46.8%) also differed in expression between Dali knockdown and control cells prior to their differentiation (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is shown by Venn diagram analysis in Figure 4E.

claim: The 428 genes that were significantly altered in expression only between stable Dali and control differentiated cells were enriched in functional categories relating to sterol biosynthesis, energy metabolism, cell cycle, response to chemical stimulus, cell cycle, adhesion and small GTPase signalling.
source: The 428 genes that were significantly altered in expression only between stable Dali and control differentiated cells were enriched in functional categories relating to sterol biosynthesis, energy metabolism, cell cycle, response to chemical stimulus, cell cycle, adhesion and small GTPase signalling (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is shown by GO enrichment analysis in Figure 4D.

claim: All 11 (of 34 known) sterol biosynthesis genes were down-regulated in Dali knockdown cells.
source: All 11 (of 34 known) sterol biosynthesis genes were down-regulated in Dali knockdown cells.
evidence: This is based on analysis of the microarray data.

claim: The down-regulation of sterol biosynthesis genes in Dali knockdown cells is consistent with the impaired neurite outgrowth because neuritogenesis and neurite outgrowth critically rely on membrane biosynthesis, and therefore, on expression of sterol biosynthesis genes.
source: This observation is consistent with the impaired neurite outgrowth of stable Dali knockdown cells because neuritogenesis and neurite outgrowth critically rely on membrane biosynthesis, and therefore, on expression of sterol biosynthesis genes (Paoletti et al., 2011).
evidence: This is inferred from the known role of sterol biosynthesis in neurite outgrowth, supported by citation.

claim: Several key neuronal differentiation genes, for example Nrcam, Dscam, Dlx1 and Pax3, were differentially expressed between Dali knockdown and control cells both prior to and after differentiation.
source: In addition, several key neuronal differentiation genes, for example Nrcam, Dscam, Dlx1 and Pax3, were differentially expressed between Dali knockdown and control cells both prior to and after differentiation.
evidence: This is based on analysis of the microarray data.

claim: 174 genes responded to RA differently depending on the presence or knockdown of Dali (FDR 5%).
source: Furthermore, multifactorial analysis of RA-induced gene expression changes in control and stable Dali knockdown cells showed that 174 genes responded to RA differently depending on the presence or knockdown of Dali (FDR 5%; Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This is based on multifactorial analysis of microarray data.

claim: Genes that responded to RA differently depending on Dali presence were significantly enriched in categories relating to neuronal development.
source: These were significantly enriched in categories relating to neuronal development (Figure 4F), including pro-differentiation factors such as the inhibitor of Wnt signaling Dkk1 (Cajanek et al., 2009) and Wnt receptor Fzd5 (Kemp et al., 2007).
evidence: This is shown by GO enrichment analysis in Figure 4F.

claim: Stable Dali knockdown cells exhibit contrasting alterations in gene expression programmes before and after RA-induced differentiation.
source: In summary, compared to control cells, stable Dali knockdown cells exhibit contrasting alterations in gene expression programmes before and after RA-induced differentiation.
evidence: This is inferred from the different sets of genes affected in proliferating vs. differentiated cells.

claim: Gene expression programmes altered in Dali knockdown cells are enriched in functional categories related to neural differentiation and function.
source: In both cases, these programmes are enriched in functional categories related to neural differentiation and function, consistent with the proposed role for Dali in neural development.
evidence: This is based on GO enrichment analysis of the microarray data.

claim: 1427 focal Dali-associated regions were discovered genome-wide using CHART-Seq.
source: We discovered 1427 focal Dali-associated regions genome-wide (Figure 5A,B; Supplementary file 5), of which all nine selected loci were validated by CHART-qPCR in an independent experiment (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is shown by CHART-seq data in Figure 5A,B.

claim: All nine selected Dali-associated loci were validated by CHART-qPCR in an independent experiment.
source: We discovered 1427 focal Dali-associated regions genome-wide (Figure 5A,B; Supplementary file 5), of which all nine selected loci were validated by CHART-qPCR in an independent experiment (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is shown by CHART-qPCR validation data in the figure supplement.

claim: Dali binding sites were typically limited to less than 1 kb in length.
source: Dali binding sites were typically limited to less than 1 kb in length (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E) and were distributed across the genome with no apparent chromosomal biases other than a depletion on the X chromosome which may reflect the inactivation of one X chromosome copy in these female N2A cells (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is shown by peak width distribution in the figure supplement.

claim: Dali binding sites were distributed across the genome with no apparent chromosomal biases other than a depletion on the X chromosome which may reflect the inactivation of one X chromosome copy in these female N2A cells.
source: Dali binding sites were typically limited to less than 1 kb in length (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E) and were distributed across the genome with no apparent chromosomal biases other than a depletion on the X chromosome which may reflect the inactivation of one X chromosome copy in these female N2A cells (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is shown by chromosomal distribution in Figure 5C.

claim: 30.5% of Dali peaks were within 5 kb of a transcriptional start site (TSS).
source: These sites were preferentially located at the 5′ end of protein coding genes (Figure 5D): 30.5% of peaks were within 5 kb of a transcriptional start site (TSS) (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is shown by distance to TSS analysis in Figure 5E.

claim: Dali bound sequences were significantly enriched for H3K4me3, H3K4me1 and H3K27ac modified histones and PolII occupancy, and were depleted for repressive histone marks.
source: Dali bound sequences were significantly enriched for H3K4me3, H3K4me1 and H3K27ac modified histones and PolII occupancy, and were depleted for repressive histone marks (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is shown by chromatin feature enrichment analysis in Figure 5F.

claim: Genes associated with Dali peaks contribute to processes related to neuronal differentiation (cell cycle), neuronal projection development (cytoskeleton organization and small GTPase mediated signal transduction), neuronal function (synaptic transmission), and more general cellular processes, such as gene expression, intracellular signalling, and cellular homeostasis.
source: GO category enrichment analysis showed that genes associated with Dali peaks contribute to processes related to neuronal differentiation (cell cycle), neuronal projection development (cytoskeleton organization and small GTPase mediated signal transduction), neuronal function (synaptic transmission), and more general cellular processes, such as gene expression, intracellular signalling, and cellular homeostasis (Figure 5G).
evidence: This is shown by GO enrichment analysis in Figure 5G.

claim: 150 genes (8.6% of all Dali bound genes) regulated by Dali contained Dali binding sites within their regulatory regions and presumably represent direct transcriptional targets.
source: 150 genes (8.6% of all Dali bound genes) regulated by Dali contained Dali binding sites within their regulatory regions (Figure 5H) and presumably represent direct transcriptional targets.
evidence: This is shown by Venn diagram analysis in Figure 5H.

claim: Dali binding sites do not exhibit significant sequence complementarity with the Dali transcript.
source: We discovered that Dali binding sites do not exhibit significant sequence complementarity with the Dali transcript (Figure 5—figure supplement 1F, see Methods), and are not likely to form RNA-DNA:DNA triplex structures (Figure 5—figure supplement 1G), suggesting that Dali does not bind DNA directly.
evidence: This is shown by computational analysis in the figure supplement.

claim: Dali binding sites are not likely to form RNA-DNA:DNA triplex structures.
source: We discovered that Dali binding sites do not exhibit significant sequence complementarity with the Dali transcript (Figure 5—figure supplement 1F, see Methods), and are not likely to form RNA-DNA:DNA triplex structures (Figure 5—figure supplement 1G), suggesting that Dali does not bind DNA directly.
evidence: This is shown by computational analysis in the figure supplement.

claim: Dali does not bind DNA directly.
source: We discovered that Dali binding sites do not exhibit significant sequence complementarity with the Dali transcript (Figure 5—figure supplement 1F, see Methods), and are not likely to form RNA-DNA:DNA triplex structures (Figure 5—figure supplement 1G), suggesting that Dali does not bind DNA directly.
evidence: This is inferred from the lack of sequence complementarity and triplex formation potential.

claim: Dali may be targeted to the genome indirectly through RNA-protein interactions.
source: We therefore speculated that Dali may be targeted to the genome indirectly thorough RNA-protein interactions.
evidence: This is speculated based on the lack of direct DNA binding evidence.

claim: 50 proteins associated with Dali, but not with antisense Dali or a size-matched unrelated control transcript, were identified using mass spectrometry.
source: To identify proteins that interact directly with Dali, we performed a pull down assay in which in vitro transcribed and 5′ end-biotinylated Dali was incubated with nuclear extract prepared from day 4 RA-differentiated ES cells. We identified, using mass spectrometry, 50 proteins that associated with Dali, but not with antisense Dali or a size-matched unrelated control transcript (Supplementary File 7).
evidence: This is based on mass spectrometry analysis of pull-down experiments.

claim: Direct interactions between the endogenous Dali transcript and DNMT1, BRG1, P66beta, and SIN3A were validated using UV-crosslinked RNA Immunoprecipitation (UV-RIP) in N2A cells.
source: Direct interactions between the endogenous Dali transcript and four of these candidate binding proteins, the DNA methyltransferase DNMT1, the BRG1 core component of the SWI/SNF family chromatin remodelling BAF complex, and the P66beta, and SIN3A transcriptional co-factors, were subsequently validated using UV-crosslinked RNA Immunoprecipitation (UV-RIP) in N2A cells (Figure 6A,B).
evidence: This is shown by UV-RIP data in Figure 6A,B.

claim: Human DALI was found to interact with human DNMT1, yet not with BRG1, in human neuroblastoma SH-SY5Y cells using UV-RIP.
source: Human DALI was also found, using UV-RIP, to interact with human DNMT1, yet not with BRG1, in human neuroblastoma SH-SY5Y cells (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is shown by UV-RIP data in Figure 6B.

claim: 9 of 58 human transcription factors reported as interacting with the DNMT1 protein were found to have binding site motifs that were significantly enriched within Dali bound CHART-seq peaks.
source: Interestingly, 9 of 58 human transcription factors reported by Hervouet et al. as interacting with the DNMT1 protein (Hervouet et al., 2010), including CTCF, but also AP-2, C-ets-1, LRH1, PARP, PAX6, STAT1, YY1, and Sp1, were found to have binding site motifs that were significantly enriched within our stringent Dali bound CHART-seq peaks (Supplementary File 6).
evidence: This is based on motif enrichment analysis and supported by citation.

claim: Motifs for none of 42 transcription factors that do not interact with DNMT1 but interact with DNMT3a and/or DNMT3b were enriched in Dali CHART-seq peaks.
source: Motifs for none of 42 transcription factors that do not interact with DNMT1 but interact with DNMT3a and/or DNMT3b (Hervouet et al., 2010) were enriched in these peaks (Supplementary File 6).
evidence: This is based on motif enrichment analysis and supported by citation.

claim: A highly-enriched CTCF-binding site-like motif was found in 125 out of 1427 Dali peaks (9%; MEME E-value = 3.1 × 10−62).
source: In particular, using a de novo motif discovery approach, we found a highly-enriched CTCF-binding site-like motif in 125 out of 1427 Dali peaks (9%; MEME E-value = 3.1 × 10−62; Figure 6C) (Supplementary File 7).
evidence: This is shown by de novo motif discovery in Figure 6C.

claim: There is a greater than expected overlap between Dali-associated regions and known CTCF binding sites in neuronal tissues.
source: This result was concordant with the greater than expected overlap between Dali-associated regions and known CTCF binding sites in neuronal tissues (Figure 5F) (Shen et al., 2012).
evidence: This is shown by enrichment analysis in Figure 5F and supported by citation.

claim: CTCF-enrichment of previously-known CTCF-binding sites within 7 Dali-bound and regulated promoters, but not at four control regions, was confirmed using ChIP-qPCR in N2A cells.
source: Using Chromatin Immunoprecipitation and qPCR (ChIP-qPCR) in N2A cells, we confirmed the CTCF-enrichment of previously-known CTCF-binding sites within 7 Dali-bound and regulated promoters, but not at four control regions (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is shown by ChIP-qPCR data in Figure 6D.

claim: UV-RIP provided no evidence of a direct physical interaction between CTCF and Dali.
source: However, despite CTCF and Dali thus occupying a subset of shared genomic binding sites, UV-RIP provided no evidence of a direct physical interaction (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is shown by UV-RIP data in Figure 6E.

claim: Dali and CTCF may be non-interacting molecular subunits of a larger ribonucleoprotein complex, or alternatively they might independently bind adjacent sequence, or compete for binding to the same region.
source: Consequently, Dali and CTCF may be non-interacting molecular subunits of a larger ribonucleoprotein complex, or alternatively they might independently bind adjacent sequence, or compete for binding to the same region.
evidence: This is speculated based on the co-localization without direct interaction.

claim: Dali is recruited to chromatin via indirect interactions with several DNA-binding proteins through its direct association with DNMT1.
source: Taken together, the data suggest that Dali is recruited to chromatin via indirect interactions with several DNA-binding proteins through its direct association with DNMT1.
evidence: This is inferred from the DNMT1 interaction, motif enrichment for DNMT1-interacting TFs, and lack of direct DNA binding.

claim: Increasing numbers of lncRNAs have been shown to direct DNA methylation changes at their sites of synthesis.
source: Increasing numbers of lncRNAs have been shown to direct DNA methylation changes at their sites of synthesis (Mohammad et al., 2010; Di Ruscio et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: The direct interaction of Dali with DNMT1 suggests that it may be able to regulate DNMT1-mediated CpG methylation at CpG island-associated promoters of Dali-bound and -regulated genes in trans.
source: The direct interaction of Dali with DNMT1, however, suggests that it may be able to regulate DNMT1-mediated CpG methylation at CpG island-associated promoters of Dali-bound and -regulated genes in trans.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the DNMT1 interaction and known function of DNMT1.

claim: Five of ten CpG islands examined by COBRA exhibited altered restriction profiles indicative of altered DNA methylation status after Dali depletion.
source: To investigate this, we performed Combined Bisulfite Restriction Analysis (COBRA) (Xiong and Laird, 1997) in parallel at 10 different CpG islands. Selection of these regions was on the basis that they each contained several COBRA-compatible restriction enzyme sites and could be efficiently amplified from bisulfite-converted template. COBRA demonstrated that five of these regions (corresponding to four genes) exhibited altered restriction profiles indicative of altered DNA methylation status after Dali depletion depletion (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is shown by COBRA data in the figure supplement.

claim: The Dlgap5, Hmgb2, and Nos1 promoters each display increased CpG methylation in two independent stable Dali knockdown lines compared to control.
source: Bisulfite sequencing demonstrating that the Dlgap5, Hmgb2, and Nos1 promoters each display increased CpG methylation in two independent stable Dali knockdown lines compared to control further confirmed these results (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is shown by bisulfite sequencing data in Figure 7A.

claim: Methylation changes upon Dali depletion occur within the core of CpG islands and are not limited to their shores.
source: Importantly, these data show that methylation changes occur within the core of these CpG islands and are not limited to their shores.
evidence: This is shown by the bisulfite sequencing data in Figure 7A.

claim: The results are consistent with Dali (or a Dali:POU3F3 complex) acting in trans, as part of a multi-subunit ribonucleoprotein complex, to reduce DNMT1-mediated CpG methylation at a subset of bound and regulated gene promoters away from its site of transcription.
source: Although other unidentified factors are also likely to play a role, our results are consistent with Dali (or a Dali:POU3F3 complex) acting in trans, as part of a multi-subunit ribonucleoprotein complex, to reduce DNMT1-mediated CpG methylation at a subset of bound and regulated gene promoters away from its site of transcription.
evidence: This is inferred from the DNMT1 interaction, trans binding, and methylation changes at distal sites.

claim: Nos1 gene has two clusters of alternative TSSs (Exon 1 and Exon 2) whose differentiated use is proposed to fine-tune its expression in response to various physiological and developmental stimuli.
source: One of these genes, Nos1, has multiple alternative promoters falling into two distinct regions (for simplicity referred to here as Exon 1 and Exon 2) whose differentiated use is proposed to fine-tune its expression in response to various physiological and developmental stimuli (Bros et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a published study.

claim: Only the 5′-most region of Nos1 contains a CpG island and is bound by Dali.
source: Only the 5′-most region contains a CpG island and is bound by Dali (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is shown by genomic annotation and CHART-seq data in Figure 7B.

claim: The expression level of the 5′ most Dali-bound Exon 1 of Nos1 was reduced, relative to that for Exon 3, when Dali was depleted, whereas the expression ratio between Exons 2 and 3 was unaffected.
source: By measuring expression levels of the three 5′-most Nos1 exons in stable Dali knockdown and control lines we observed that the expression level of the 5′ most Dali-bound Exon 1 was reduced, relative to that for Exon 3, when Dali was depleted, whereas the expression ratio between Exons 2 and 3 was unaffected (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is shown by qRT-PCR data in Figure 7C.

claim: Dali may function by promoting the preferential use of a distantly located (and more rarely used) alternative promoter potentially through its effect on promoter-associated CpG island methylation.
source: The preferential use of the 5′ most CpG site could reflect a secondary effect of Dali knockdown. Nevertheless, the observation that this site is bound by Dali transcript suggests that Dali may function by promoting the preferential use of a distantly located (and more rarely used) alternative promoter potentially through its effect on promoter-associated CpG island methylation.
evidence: This is inferred from the Dali binding, methylation changes, and differential exon usage.

claim: A recognisable binding motif for POU III family transcription factors, such as POU3F3, was present in 115 out of 1427 Dali CHART-Seq peaks (8.0%; E-value = 3.8 × 10−5).
source: A recognisable binding motif for POU III family transcription factors, such as POU3F3, was present in 115 out of 1427 Dali CHART-Seq peaks (8.0%; E-value = 3.8 × 10−5; Figure 6F).
evidence: This is shown by de novo motif discovery in Figure 6F.

claim: Dali occupies regulatory regions within 135 (13%) of Pou3f3 targets.
source: This finding, together with Dali and Pou3f3 regulating a set of common genes (Figure 3D) and Dali occupying regulatory regions within 135 (13%) of Pou3f3 targets (Figure 5H), suggested that Dali and POU3F3 protein may interact physically.
evidence: This is shown by Venn diagram analysis in Figure 5H.

claim: Direct RNA-protein interactions were observed between over-expressed FLAG-tagged POU3F3 and co-transfected Dali, using UV-RIP in N2A cells.
source: Indeed, we observed direct RNA-protein interactions between over-expressed FLAG-tagged POU3F3 and co-transfected Dali, using UV-RIP in N2A cells (Figure 6G).
evidence: This is shown by UV-RIP data in Figure 6G.

claim: At least five genes that were regulated by both Dali and Pou3f3 contained regions that were bound both by Dali and by POU3F3 protein.
source: Using ChIP-qPCR, we then determined that at least five genes that were regulated by both Dali and Pou3f3 contained regions that were bound both by Dali and by POU3F3 protein (Figure 6H).
evidence: This is shown by ChIP-qPCR data in Figure 6H.

claim: Dali and POU3F3 form a complex that binds to and regulates a subset of genes in trans in N2A cells.
source: These results provide further mechanistic insights into Dali's mode of action and indicate that Dali and POU3F3 form a complex that binds to and regulates a subset of genes in trans in N2A cells.
evidence: This is inferred from the physical interaction, co-occupancy, and co-regulation data.

claim: De novo expressed Dali transcript from its endogenous locus in E14 mouse ES cells significantly increased Pou3f3 expression after 72 hr.
source: To achieve this, we induced Dali expression from its endogenous locus in E14 mouse ES cells, which do not express Dali or Pou3f3 to detectable levels, using transient transfection of an artificial Transcription Activator-Like effector (TALE) transcription factor. After 72 hr, up-regulation of Dali transcript was shown to significantly increase Pou3f3 expression (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is shown by TALE-mediated induction and qRT-PCR data in Figure 7D.

claim: Dali expression from its own locus is sufficient to induce the expression of its genomically neighbouring Pou3f3 gene.
source: Dali expression from its own locus is thus sufficient to induce the expression of its genomically neighbouring Pou3f3 gene (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is shown by TALE-mediated induction data in Figure 7D.

claim: Dali up-regulation reduced E2f2 transcript levels by approximately 40%.
source: We next investigated the expression levels of E2f2, a gene that we found to be negatively regulated by Dali using shRNA mediated knockdown (Supplementary file 2), and found that Dali up-regulation reduced E2f2 transcript levels by approximately 40% (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is shown by TALE-mediated induction and qRT-PCR data in Figure 7D.

claim: Dali can regulate both local and distal target genes when its expression is induced from its endogenous locus.
source: Taken together, these results indicate that Dali can regulate both local and distal target genes when its expression is induced from its endogenous locus.
evidence: This is inferred from the TALE-mediated induction showing regulation of both Pou3f3 (local) and E2f2 (distal).

claim: The ability of nuclear localised lncRNAs to act in trans at distal genomic locations to regulate gene expression programs has been poorly understood.
source: The ability of nuclear localised lncRNAs to act in trans at distal genomic locations to regulate gene expression programs has been poorly understood.
evidence: This is presented as a knowledge gap in the field.

claim: Direct transcriptional targets of only a small number of trans-acting lncRNAs (for example, Paupar (mouse), HOTAIR, NEAT1, TERC, RMST (all human), and rox2 (Drosophila)) have been identified.
source: This is in large part because the direct transcriptional targets of only a small number of such transcripts (for example, Paupar (mouse), HOTAIR, NEAT1, TERC, RMST (all human), and rox2 (Drosophila)) have been identified thus far (Chu et al., 2011; Simon et al., 2011; Ng et al., 2013; Vance et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: It has been unclear how trans-acting lncRNAs are targeted to distal functional elements and whether thereafter they alter chromatin structure in situ.
source: Consequently, it has been unclear how these transcripts are targeted to distal functional elements and whether thereafter they alter chromatin structure in situ.
evidence: This is presented as a knowledge gap that the study addresses.

claim: Dali acts both locally to regulate the expression of its nearest protein-coding gene, Pou3f3, and distally to regulate both Pou3f3-dependent and -independent target genes in an RNA-dependent manner.
source: In this study we found evidence that the intergenic lncRNA Dali acts both locally to regulate the expression of its nearest protein-coding gene, Pou3f3, and distally to regulate both Pou3f3-dependent and -independent target genes in an RNA-dependent manner.
evidence: This is based on the combined knockdown, CHART-seq, and expression analysis data.

claim: 8.8% (150) of all genes whose expression altered following Dali depletion were associated with Dali binding sites within 1 Mb and are likely to represent direct regulatory targets.
source: 8.8% (150) of all genes whose expression altered following Dali depletion were associated with Dali binding sites within 1 Mb (although 30% of peaks reside within 5 kb of a TSS, see Figure 5E) and, therefore, are likely to represent direct regulatory targets.
evidence: This is based on integration of CHART-seq and expression data.

claim: The proportion of functional Dali binding sites (8.8%) lies within the range of functional sites observed for transcription factors.
source: This proportion lies within the range of functional sites observed for transcription factors (Cusanovich et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a published study.

claim: Mouse or human Dali is recruited to chromatin indirectly via RNA-protein interactions with both sequence-specific transcription factor proteins, such as POU3F3, or non-sequence specific DNA binding cofactors including DNMT1, which in turn may interact with sequence-specific DNA-binding proteins.
source: Our results are consistent with a model in which mouse or human Dali is recruited to chromatin indirectly via RNA-protein interactions with both sequence-specific transcription factor proteins, such as POU3F3 which is encoded by its neighbouring gene, or non-sequence specific DNA binding cofactors including DNMT1, which in turn may interact with sequence-specific DNA-binding proteins.
evidence: This is a model inferred from the protein interaction, motif enrichment, and binding data.

claim: Pou3f3-dependent target genes are regulated by Dali both indirectly, via its transcriptional regulatory effect on the Pou3f3 gene, and directly via its physical interaction with the POU3F3 protein and their co-occupancy at regulatory regions of target genes.
source: In this model, Pou3f3-dependent target genes are regulated by Dali both indirectly, via its transcriptional regulatory effect on the Pou3f3 gene, and directly via its physical interaction with the POU3F3 protein and their co-occupancy at regulatory regions of target genes.
evidence: This is a model inferred from the multiple lines of evidence showing Dali-Pou3f3 interactions.

claim: Both human and mouse Dali associate with DNMT1 and depletion of Dali levels increases CpG methylation at Dali bound and regulated promoters in trans.
source: Our data show that both human and mouse Dali associate with DNMT1 and that depletion of Dali levels increases CpG methylation at Dali bound and regulated promoters in trans.
evidence: This is based on UV-RIP and bisulfite sequencing data.

claim: A growing body of literature has implicated lncRNAs, such as Kcnq1ot1 and ecCEBPA, in modulating CpG methylation in a DNMT1-dependent manner at their sites of synthesis.
source: Whilst a growing body of literature has implicated lncRNAs, such as Kcnq1ot1 and ecCEBPA (Mohammad et al., 2010; Di Ruscio et al., 2013), in modulating CpG methylation in a DNMT1-dependent manner at their sites of synthesis, our findings represent the first evidence that an intergenic lncRNA can regulate DNA methylation in trans at distal genomic locations away from its site of transcription.
evidence: This is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: The findings represent the first evidence that an intergenic lncRNA can regulate DNA methylation in trans at distal genomic locations away from its site of transcription.
source: Whilst a growing body of literature has implicated lncRNAs, such as Kcnq1ot1 and ecCEBPA (Mohammad et al., 2010; Di Ruscio et al., 2013), in modulating CpG methylation in a DNMT1-dependent manner at their sites of synthesis, our findings represent the first evidence that an intergenic lncRNA can regulate DNA methylation in trans at distal genomic locations away from its site of transcription.
evidence: This is based on the novel combination of trans binding and methylation regulation shown in this study.

claim: Dali inhibits DNA methylation at a subset of bound and regulated regions, presumably deposited by the DNMT1 DNA methyltransferase, to which it binds.
source: Our findings suggest that Dali inhibits DNA methylation at a subset of bound and regulated regions, presumably deposited by the DNMT1 DNA methyltransferase, to which it binds.
evidence: This is inferred from the increased methylation upon Dali depletion and the DNMT1 interaction.

claim: DNMT1 binds structured RNA with higher affinity than its DNA substrate.
source: DNMT1 binds structured RNA with higher affinity than its DNA substrate (Di Ruscio et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a published study.

claim: It is possible that Dali competes for binding to DNMT1 with either protein co-factors such as UHRF1, which loads and orients the enzyme on the DNA substrate, or its DNA substrate.
source: It is thus possible that Dali competes for binding to DNMT1 with either protein co-factors such as UHRF1, which loads and orients the enzyme on the DNA substrate (Inomata et al., 2008), or its DNA substrate.
evidence: This is a hypothesis about the mechanism, supported by citation about UHRF1 function.

claim: Targeting of DNMT1 to specific loci is believed to be mediated by DNMT1-interacting transcription factors.
source: Targeting of DNMT1 to specific loci is believed to be mediated by DNMT1-interacting transcription factors.
evidence: This is presented as established knowledge in the field.

claim: 58 transcriptional factors have been reported as DNMT1 interactors, of which 9 have enriched sequence motifs in Dali CHART-Seq peaks.
source: 58 transcriptional factors have been reported as DNMT1 interactors (Hervouet et al., 2010), of which 9 have enriched sequence motifs in Dali CHART-Seq peaks.
evidence: This is based on motif enrichment analysis and supported by citation.

claim: Transcription factors promote the sequence-specificity of Dali-modulated DNA methylation changes.
source: We thus propose a model in which such transcription factors promote the sequence-specificity of Dali-modulated DNA methylation changes.
evidence: This is a proposed model based on the motif enrichment and DNMT1 interaction data.

claim: Dali regulates genes involved in neural development and function.
source: We have shown that Dali regulates genes involved in neural development and function and its depletion disrupts terminal stages of neuronal differentiation, more particularly neurite outgrowth development.
evidence: This is based on GO enrichment analysis and neurite outgrowth assays.

claim: Dali RNA binds to and up-regulates the promoters or promoter-proximal regions of key pro-differentiation factors, such as E2f2, Fam5b, Sparc and Dkk1.
source: Dali RNA binds to and up-regulates the promoters or promoter-proximal regions of key pro-differentiation factors, such as E2f2 (Persengiev et al., 2001), Fam5b (Terashima et al., 2010), Sparc (Bhoopathi et al., 2011) and Dkk1 (Cajanek et al., 2009) (Watanabe et al., 2005), as well as binding and negatively regulating genes such as Kif2c and Kif11 which are known to block neurite outgrowth (Laketa et al., 2007; Myers and Baas, 2007; Nadar et al., 2012).
evidence: This is based on CHART-seq and expression data, with citations supporting the functional roles of these genes.

claim: Dali binds and negatively regulates genes such as Kif2c and Kif11 which are known to block neurite outgrowth.

evidence: This is based on CHART-seq and expression data, with citations supporting the functional roles of these genes.

claim: Dali works as a pro-differentiation factor in neural development by regulating the balance between proliferation and differentiation, as well as processes associated with terminal neuronal differentiation.
source: Therefore, Dali works as a pro-differentiation factor in neural development by regulating the balance between proliferation and differentiation, as well as processes associated with terminal neuronal differentiation.
evidence: This is inferred from the combined functional and expression data.

claim: Dali is unusual in acting in a transcript-dependent manner to perform both local and distal gene regulatory roles like another such lncRNA, Paupar.
source: Dali is unusual in acting in a transcript-dependent manner to perform both local and distal gene regulatory roles like another such lncRNA, Paupar (Vance et al., 2014).
evidence: This is based on comparison with published work on Paupar, supported by citation.

claim: Both Dali and Paupar lncRNAs are CNS-expressed and evolutionarily constrained transcripts that are co-expressed with their neighbouring transcription factor genes both spatially and temporally.
source: Dali is transcribed in the vicinity of a neuronal transcription factor Pou3f3. Both Dali and Paupar lncRNAs are CNS-expressed and evolutionarily constrained transcripts that are co-expressed with their neighbouring transcription factor genes both spatially and temporally.
evidence: This is based on expression and conservation data for Dali and comparison with published Paupar data.

claim: Both Dali and Paupar lncRNAs interact directly with the protein product of their neighbouring genes, POU3F3 and PAX6, respectively, to regulate a large set of targets in trans.
source: Moreover, both lncRNAs interact directly with the protein product of their neighbouring genes, POU3F3 and PAX6, respectively, to regulate a large set of targets in trans.
evidence: This is based on UV-RIP data for Dali and comparison with published Paupar data.

claim: lncRNAs may commonly interact with the product of genomically adjacent transcription factor genes to act in trans on distal genes.
source: These observations, together with the preferential genomic location of intergenic lncRNA loci adjacent to transcription factor genes (Ponjavic et al., 2009) imply that lncRNAs may commonly interact with the product of genomically adjacent transcription factor genes to act in trans on distal genes.
evidence: This is a hypothesis inferred from the observations about Dali and Paupar, supported by citation about genomic organization.
